stories.title: Increased southward swings of the South Indian convergence zone under greenhouse warming
stories.description: Extreme southward swings of the South Indian convergence zone can induce devastating floods over parts of southern Africa. How greenhouse warming affects such southward swings is not well understood. Here we show that, under a high-emissions scenario, the frequency of extreme southward swings doubles from one event per 22 years in the twentieth century to one per 10 years in the twenty-first century with an average increase in rainfall intensity of 20%. The increased frequency is related to faster warming of the African continent than of the Indian Ocean that intensifies northerly winds, and to a poleward migration of Southern Ocean westerlies that drives a pattern of faster subtropical Indian Ocean warming to the south and enhances Atlantic-to-Africa moisture transport, both of which favour a southward swing of the South Indian convergence zone. More frequent southward migration of the South Indian convergence zone might thus indicate increasing flooding risk in parts of southern Africa. Extreme southward swings of the South Indian convergence zone can lead to severe rainfall and flooding in southern Africa. Here the authors show that climate change leads to an increase in the frequency and intensity of such swings.

stories.title: Traits associated with novel foraging success in urban mesopredators
stories.description: Urbanization is transforming ecosystems worldwide, creating novel environmental conditions that wildlife must adjust to. Because urban species differ markedly in ecological strategies, functional traits, and societal perceptions, they experience divergent pressures that shape their responses to the challenges associated with city living. A comparative framework can therefore reveal how both individual and species-level differences influence behaviors such as risk-taking and problem solving, even among related taxa in the same habitat. Here, we challenged free-ranging mesopredators with a novel foraging task and predicted a gradient of species-specific behavioral responses, hypothesizing that boldness, exploration, and effort would influence problem-solving success within and across species. We collected data from 110 locations across the East Bay of California for five mesopredator species: raccoons, opossums, striped skunks, coyotes, and domestic cats. Individuals from all species solved the task multiple times, but raccoons and coyotes emerged as the most successful despite divergent approaches. Across species, effort was the strongest predictor of success, whereas within species, exploratory individuals were most likely to solve. In contrast, boldness did not predict success. These results illustrate how trait differences within and among a taxonomic guild shape behavioral responses to novel challenges, offering insights on the strategies that facilitate urban persistence.

stories.title: Light-induced asymmetric pseudogap below the critical temperature in cuprates
stories.description: High-temperature cuprate superconductors remain a key platform for studying the competition and coexistence of emergent quantum phases of matter. These include non-s-wave superconductivity with a high transition temperature, non-Fermi-liquid transport and the pseudogap regime. How superconductivity emerges alongside and competes with the pseudogap remains an open question. Here, by directly accessing the near-antinodal region of optimally doped Bi-based cuprates via time- and angle-resolved photoemission, we report a transient change from a symmetric superconducting-like density of states to an asymmetric pseudogap-like density of states when superconductivity is disrupted by a sufficiently high excitation fluence. We observe this change at electronic temperatures well below the equilibrium superconducting critical temperature. Conversely, when superconductivity is fully restored, the pseudogap is suppressed, as indicated by a particle–hole-symmetric density of states. We also observe the coexistence of pseudogap and superconducting features at intermediate times or intermediate fluence. Our findings challenge the view that superconductivity emerges from phase coherence in the pseudogap. Instead, we show that the two states compete and that the low-temperature ground state of cuprates reflects an interplay between the superconducting and pseudogap states. How superconductivity relates to the pseudogap in cuprates remains unclear. Now, time-resolved photoemission measurements show a light-induced pseudogap-like state below critical temperature, revealing a dynamic interplay with superconductivity.

stories.title: Exploring healthy aging through preclinical Alzheimer disease in the Knight Alzheimer Research Imaging dataset
stories.description: Alzheimer disease (AD) remains a significant global public health challenge, requiring robust multimodal datasets to elucidate its prolonged preclinical phase, improve early detection, advance understanding of disease trajectories, and guide intervention strategies. Here we present the Knight Alzheimer Research Imaging (KARI) dataset, established by the Washington University Knight ADRC to address this critical need. We detail comprehensive multimodal neuroimaging from 1,645 participants (aged 42-97) across 6,217 acquisitions. Spanning the AD spectrum from healthy aging to symptomatic disease, the cohort undergoes extensive longitudinal imaging using structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) alongside positron emission tomography (PET) tracers for amyloid and tau pathology. This is complemented by rich clinical, cognitive, genetic, and biomarker data. In addition to raw imaging, the dataset provides quality-controlled processed outputs, including anatomical segmentations and biomarker quantification. By making this data accessible to researchers, the Knight ADRC aims to accelerate discoveries in pathophysiology, biomarker identification, and therapeutic development. The KARI dataset maps healthy aging through preclinical Alzheimer disease across >6,000 scans from 1,645 adults. Demonstrating its utility, imaging biomarkers scale with clinical severity, providing a resource to accelerate future Alzheimer research.

stories.title: Lagrangian-Eulerian learning of flow field and trajectories with TrajectoryFlowNet
stories.description: Predicting particle transport in complex flows is traditionally achieved by solving the Navier–Stokes equations. Numerical and experimental methods typically require deep physical insights and incur high computational costs. Although machine learning offers an alternative, existing approaches fail to generalize the prediction of long-range particle trajectories in sparse data regimes. Here, to this end, we propose TrajectoryFlowNet, a Lagrangian–Eulerian physics-informed neural network architecture, for fluid flow velocimetry and imaging via learning to predict spatiotemporal flow fields and long-range particle trajectories. The salient features of our model include its ability to handle complex flow patterns with irregular boundaries, predict the full-field flows, image the long-range flow trajectory of any arbitrary particle, and ensure physical consistency in predictions based on only scarce measurement of flow trajectories. We validate TrajectoryFlowNet via both numerical examples (for example, lid-driven cavity flow and complex cylinder flow) and experimental test cases (for example, aortic and ventricle blood flows) across diverse flow scenarios. The results demonstrate our model’s effectiveness in capturing intricate particle-laden flow dynamics, enabling long-range tracking of particles and accurate construction of flow fields in real-world applications. Wan et al. introduce a physics-informed learning model that simultaneously predicts long-range particle paths and flow fields based on very limited trajectory measurements, validated in both simulations and blood-flow experiments.

stories.title: Enhancing language learning with AI: the role of AI service quality in learning satisfaction and performance in mobile-assisted language learning applications
stories.description: Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered mobile-assisted language learning (MALL) applications are transforming the traditional language learning paradigm by leveraging AI technologies to provide a more efficient, convenient, and personalized learning experience. Despite the integration of AI technologies into MALL applications, prior studies have overlooked the critical role of AI service quality in shaping learners’ learning satisfaction levels and performance within these applications. This study addresses this research gap by leveraging social support theory to develop a research model that examines how the AI service quality of AI-powered MALL applications influences social support, specifically informational, emotional, and appraisal support. These forms of support are further analyzed to determine their effects on learners’ learning satisfaction levels and performance. A total of 978 valid samples were collected from users of AI-powered MALL applications and analyzed using the partial least-squares method. The results indicate that AI service quality significantly enhances users’ perceptions of informational, emotional, and appraisal support. These forms of support positively influence learning satisfaction and learning performance. Furthermore, the mediation analysis revealed that informational, emotional, and appraisal support act as partial mediators in the relationships between AI service quality and learning satisfaction and between AI service quality and learning performance. This study contributes to the literature by revealing how AI service quality, social support, and learning satisfaction and performance interact in the context of AI-enabled MALL applications. We also offer practical insights for improving the user experience and maximizing the learning outcomes of AI-driven MALL applications.

stories.title: Directed assembly of cathode interlayers enables efficient binary organic solar cells
stories.description: Cathode interlayers create interfacial dipoles in organic solar cells to maximize device efficiency. However, the dipoles are highly dependent on the molecular orientation of the interlayers, which remain challenging to be controlled. Here, based on the amphiphilic nature of the interlayers, we show a stepwise film deposition approach using a polar solvent for active layer pretreatment and a bipolar solvent for subsequent interlayer self assembly. Sum-frequency generation vibrational spectroscopy reveals a preferred perpendicular orientation of the interlayer molecules, thereby enhancing the surface potential and reducing the charge transport resistance. As a result, we achieve a certified efficiency of 20.65% and fill factor of 82.7% in binary organic solar cells. This method is universally applicable to different cathode interlayers and active layers. Our work highlights the importance of controlling interlayer molecular orientation for unlocking significant performance gains, paving the way for further advancements in device optimization. Cathode interlayers play a pivotal role in improving the performance of organic solar cells. Yao, Zhang, Zhang, Wang et al. show a stepwise solvent treatment to achieve a vertically aligned cathode interlayer, enabling a certified efficiency of 20.65% in binary organic solar cells.
